input: An amine absorption unit was tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln. Over 60 days at 9 t of carbon dioxide per day, the unit captured 86% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. The capture figure is the share of the carbon dioxide entering with the treated gas that the solvent took up, and the daily rate is the throughput at which the unit ran for the full test period. Steam demand was 3.4 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured; solvent loss was 2.4 kg per tonne captured. The two operating figures rest on the same basis, per tonne captured, and can be read together: steam demand is the energy cost of regenerating the solvent, and solvent loss is the material cost of running the unit on this gas. The test establishes the capture share and both operating figures at pilot scale over a run of the stated length, on kiln gas as received. Beyond 60 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent is untested. Kiln dust reaches the solvent with the gas, and a longer run would show whether dust builds up in the solvent or degrades its performance in service; the present results carry no evidence on that point, and the figures stand for the tested period only, at the stated rate and on the stated gas.
